findings.question: q-trigonometry-angles-and-radian-measure-0013
findings.quote: This doubles the computed angle. Using diameter instead of radius can change ratios. Divide arc length by the stated radius.
findings.problem: The note for 120 degrees suggests using the diameter instead of the radius, but that gives (8π/3)/16 = π/6 radians = 30 degrees, not 120 degrees. It teaches a mismatched cause for this wrong answer.
findings.fix: Explain that using 360 degrees per π radian gives 120 degrees because it confuses a full turn with a half-turn; check that π radians equals 180 degrees.

findings.question: q-trigonometry-angles-and-radian-measure-0017
findings.quote: This treats half a radian as half a turn. Both contain a half. Compare it with pi over two.
findings.problem: The note for Quadrant II names a mistake that does not produce Quadrant II. Half a turn is π radians, which ends on the negative x-axis and is outside all quadrants.
findings.fix: Explain that overestimating the size of a radian can make the angle seem greater than 90 degrees; check that 0.5 is less than π/2, the Quadrant I boundary.
